Ah, the predictable theatrics of the insecure, this knee-jerk impulse to swat at the unfamiliar, to dismiss Manus with a careless sneer, branding it a mere ‘Claude wrapper,’ as if innovation were the exclusive preserve of one hemisphere! But let us pause, if we are still capable, and consider: those who have engaged with this creation, those who have witnessed its workings, speak not in the language of derision but of discovery. They proclaim its efficacy, its latent force, its singularity in a market otherwise teeming with echoes of itself.

And so the question stands, what frightens us so? That the Chinese have dared? That they have built and released it, unshackled by our conditioned condescension? The world moves forward, and it is enriched, not diminished, by this latest addition to the arsenal of human ingenuity. We, the self-anointed custodians of technological supremacy, are left with a choice: to carp and cower in the shadow of our own complacency, or to rise yes, rise! and meet this provocation with the only response worthy of an intelligent people: greater audacity, deeper resolve, an unwavering commitment to our own forward march.

comments.text:
The fact that you keep running out of tokens means that it is expensive inefficient hype. If you can't do a simple task in a cost efficient way, thats part of the product offering and it counts. Influencers need to take more responsibility for turning down money and free access to these unproven companies, especially ones that don't even develop their own models.

 Looking from the outside, it appears to me that they have done a couple of really sleazy things which is first give beta access only to a select group of influencers that they figured would hype their company, and then plant stories that the beta invitations were being resold for thousands of dollars. I don't even believe there is a multi million person waiting list. Theres no way to even verify that claim.

The fact that pretty much all the companies are using similar marketing tactics at the moment is what is making the whole industry such a shitshow. The consumer cannot trust that the product actually works, which is kind of a given in every other industry. 

Its kinda tough to be a Youtuber, because you need to make a video about the latest buzz to get paid yourself, so the hype companies get rewarded, and so do the influencers. The people getting shafted by this are millions of normal people who have their time wasted by overhyped unproven products, and buggy software pushed as the next AGI. In time this will affect some of the influencers, but the worst of them will be onto the next big thing. I have to believe that there will be a more long term and more sustainable career for people that turn down relationships with disreputable companies, and tell their subscribers the truth. History always repeats itself, but it does take some time.
